title: Adore: Differentially Oblivious Relational Database Operators
review_status: full-text audit complete; operator proofs/model, fixed-size one-record adjacency, SGX threat boundary, benchmark scale and latency, comparator gap, and acknowledged composition limitation checked; Doquet follow-up full text checked
sections_checked: Abstract and contribution claims
Threat model and Definition 2.1
Theorems for filtering, groupby, and foreign-key join
Section 5: Intel SGX/BDB experimental setup, baselines, timings and latency breakdown
Discussion/conclusion: composition and SGX side-channel limits
evidence_note: Reports up to 7.4x vs. fully-oblivious ObliDB for a foreign-key join case, but 98.1–182.1x overhead vs non-oblivious Spark SQL; complex operator composition is outside the evaluation. Threat model does not hide private-enclave cache access; known SGX side channels are out of scope. Doquet later provides static select-join composition and a stronger private-memory observer model, but leaves updates and privacy-budget/index selection open.

title: PrivLava: Synthesizing Relational Data with Foreign Keys under Differential Privacy
review_status: full-text audit complete; latent-FK model, supported DAG/public-private cases, census and modified TPC-H aggregate-query evaluations, runtime, and small-data/privacy-budget limitation checked; PrivPetal primary abstract/publication checked as targeted follow-up
sections_checked: Abstract and relational problem setting
Sections 3–6: latent graphical model, FK DAG and public relation support, privacy accounting
Section 7: census/TPC-H settings, aggregate-query error and computation cost
Conclusion and explicit sample-size/noise limitation
venue_year_verified: Proceedings of the ACM on Management of Data 1(2), SIGMOD/PODS 2023; DOI 10.1145/3589287
evidence_note: Latent-variable graphical models model FK-induced correlations and support FK DAGs and public/private relations. On California and Île-de-France census data and modified TPC-H it improves selected aggregate-query accuracy over the tested DP synthesis baselines; reported run can take up to 12 hours and small data can leave latent marginals noise-dominated. PrivPetal (2025) directly targets PrivLava's repeated-EM privacy-budget cost; its full tables were not reviewed in this audit.

title: Practical and Asymptotically Optimal Quantization of High-Dimensional Vectors in Euclidean Space for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
review_status: full-text audit complete; estimator/code extension, staged distance evaluation, six-dataset benchmark, hardware/thread settings, IVF scope, index-build results and graph-index limitation checked; MRQ official PVLDB full paper checked as later comparator
sections_checked: Abstract and asymptotic error/space formulation
Sections 3–4: extended code, error bound and staged distance estimate
Section 5: datasets, baselines, recall/QPS, index and quantization setup
Sections 6–7: related methods, conclusion and graph-index future-work boundary
evidence_note: Extended RaBitQ supports 1–10 bits/dimension and staged distance estimates. Six datasets include about 113.5M MS MARCO vectors; quantization example uses 96 threads/48 cores, while ANN query measurements are single-threaded. The reported two-hour quantization at 9 bits is setup-specific; IVF build exceeded one day. Efficient graph-index integration is left for future work. MRQ (PVLDB 2026) uses PCA/projection and compares IVF/HNSW; it reports favorable gains on many but not all tested embedding datasets.

title: Doquet: Differentially Oblivious Range and Join Queries with Private Data Structures
review_status: targeted citation follow-up; official PVLDB full text checked for functionality, composition, static-data assumption, index/privacy-budget management gap, and experiment framing

evidence_note: Directly advances Adore beyond isolated operators by supporting select-join and an observer that can eavesdrop on private-memory accesses. Supports the conclusion that composition was partially achieved; system assumes static data and leaves updates and privacy-budget/index selection open.

title: PrivPetal: Relational Data Synthesis via Permutation Relations
review_status: targeted citation follow-up; primary arXiv abstract and ACM publication metadata checked; full text and experimental tables not audited
sections_checked: Primary arXiv abstract: stated PrivLava privacy-cost motivation, permutation-relation approach and aggregate-query evaluation claim
PACMMOD/SIGMOD 2025 publication metadata
evidence_note: Authors identify repeated EM iterations in PrivLava as potentially prohibitive in privacy-budget consumption and propose permutation relations plus a refined Markov random field. Primary abstract reports better aggregate-query accuracy on multiple real datasets and TPC-H; no independent replication or common-budget comparison was performed here.

title: Quantization Meets Projection: A Happy Marriage for Approximate k-Nearest Neighbor Search
review_status: targeted follow-up; official PVLDB 2026 full paper inspected for MRQ method, eight datasets, IVF/HNSW/RaBitQ comparisons, per-dataset reversals, and stated distributed-work future
sections_checked: Introduction: fixed-dimensional quantization limitation and MRQ proposal
Experiment settings, eight datasets, IVF-RaBitQ/MRQ/HNSW baselines
Per-dataset performance and OpenAI embedding reversal
Conclusion/future work
evidence_note: MRQ combines projection, quantized projected dimensions and residual statistics. On eight public datasets it reports up to 3.4x speedup with one-sixth the bits on OpenAI-3072; HNSW is faster on OpenAI-1536/3072 at equivalent recall, so the headline gain is not uniform. Full technical report contains additional comparisons not audited here.
